metadata.name: Meat Church BBQ Recipe Collection
metadata.description: BBQ recipes from Meat Church featuring their award-winning rubs and seasonings

recipes.name: Texas Style Brisket
recipes.description: Classic Texas style brisket smoked low and slow. The cornerstone of Meat Church BBQ.

steps.name: Trim brisket
steps.instruction: Trim excess fat and silver skin off the top. Remove any hard pieces of fat that won't render. Trim fat on bottom leaving only 1/4 inch.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Apply Holy Cow rub to meat side, then come back with Holy Gospel in a 70/30 ratio. Let seasoning adhere 30 minutes.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Prepare smoker at 250°F using post oak or hickory. Place brisket fat side down. Smoke until internal temp reaches 165°F, about 6-8 hours. Wrap in butcher paper. Continue cooking until probe tender at 200-205°F. Rest 1-2 hours before slicing.

recipes.name: Mexican Brisket
recipes.description: Beef version of the wildly popular Mexican Pulled Pork. Marinated in pickled jalapeño juice for amazing flavor.

steps.name: Marinate
steps.instruction: Place trimmed brisket in container. Pour pickled jalapeño juice over brisket. Marinate overnight in refrigerator.

steps.name: Season and smoke
steps.instruction: Remove from marinade and pat dry. Season liberally with Dia de la Fajita. Smoke at 250°F until probe tender at 200-205°F.

food.name: Meat Church Dia de la Fajita rub

recipes.name: Pulled Pork
recipes.description: Sweet pulled pork - the BBQ Matt grew up on. Simple, easy, and fantastic.

steps.name: Prep and season
steps.instruction: Trim excess fat from pork butt. Apply yellow mustard as binder. Season liberally with Honey Hog rub on all sides.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Prepare smoker at 275°F with hickory or pecan. Smoke until internal temp reaches 205°F and probe slides in like butter, about 8 hours. Rest 30 minutes, then pull with forks or meat claws.

recipes.name: Hickory Pulled Pork
recipes.description: Pulled pork using Hickory AP seasoning for a savory flavor profile.

steps.name: Prep and season
steps.instruction: Trim pork butt. Season liberally with Hickory AP on all sides. Let sit 30 minutes.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Prepare smoker at 250°F with hickory. Smoke until probe tender above 200°F. Pull and serve.

recipes.name: No Wrap Pork Butt
recipes.description: Low and slow method for insane bark without wrapping. Perfect for pellet grills.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Season pork butt with Holy Gospel or your preferred rub.

steps.name: Smoke low and slow
steps.instruction: Prepare smoker at 200°F. Smoke for approximately 12 hours until probe tender. The lower temp elongates cook time building incredible bark.

recipes.name: North Carolina Style Pulled Pork
recipes.description: Classic southern BBQ with Cheerwine BBQ sauce and sweet coleslaw.

steps.name: Brine and season
steps.instruction: Brine pork butt overnight in Meat Church brine. Pat dry and season with Honey Hog.

steps.name: Smoke and sauce
steps.instruction: Smoke at 250°F with hickory, pecan, or cherry until probe tender. Serve with Cheerwine BBQ sauce.

recipes.name: Sweet Honey Baby Back Ribs
recipes.description: Fall-off-the-bone baby back ribs with sweet honey glaze.

steps.name: Prep ribs
steps.instruction: Remove membrane from back of ribs. Apply mustard as binder and season liberally with Honey Hog.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 250°F for 3 hours. Wrap in foil with honey and butter. Cook 1.5 hours more. Unwrap and glaze with BBQ sauce. Cook 30 more minutes.

recipes.name: Memphis Style Dry Rub Ribs
recipes.description: Super simple cook that lets the rub shine. No sauce needed.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Remove membrane. Season heavily with Holy Gospel on both sides.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 275°F for 4-5 hours until meat pulls back from bones. No wrap, no sauce - just dry rub perfection.

recipes.name: Texas Style Spare Ribs
recipes.description: Central Texas style spare ribs with bold pepper flavor.

steps.name: Prep and season
steps.instruction: Trim spare ribs St. Louis style. Season with Holy Cow for pepper-forward Texas flavor.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 275°F with post oak for 5-6 hours until bark is set and meat is tender.

recipes.name: Beef Party Ribs
recipes.description: Beef chuck ribs, aka 'Brisket on a stick'. Rich, beefy, and impressive.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Season beef chuck ribs on all sides with Holy Gospel. Let adhere 15 minutes to 1 hour.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Prepare smoker at 250°F with post oak, mesquite, hickory, or pecan. Smoke until probe tender, about 6 hours.

steps.name: Glaze
steps.instruction: Glaze with Bourbon BBQ sauce in final 30 minutes if desired.

recipes.name: Beef Back Ribs
recipes.description: Tender beef back ribs with simple seasoning.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Remove membrane from back of ribs. Season with Holy Cow.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 275°F for 3-4 hours until meat pulls back from bones and is probe tender.

recipes.name: Smashburger
recipes.description: Simple technique that lets beef and crust shine. Favorite burger style.

steps.name: Form balls
steps.instruction: Divide ground beef into 4 portions. Form into loose balls. Season with Holy Cow.

steps.name: Smash and cook
steps.instruction: Heat griddle or cast iron over high heat. Place ball on griddle, smash flat with spatula. Cook 2-3 minutes until crispy edges. Flip, add cheese, cook 1 more minute.

steps.name: Serve
steps.instruction: Serve on toasted buns with desired toppings.

recipes.name: Crack Burgers
recipes.description: Mount Rushmore worthy burgers with ranch and bacon. Made with NFL QB Jarrett Stidham.

steps.name: Mix meat
steps.instruction: Combine ground beef with sour cream, ranch mix, and Blanco seasoning. Mix gently and form into 6 patties.

steps.name: Cook
steps.instruction: Cook on griddle over medium-high heat 4-5 minutes per side. Top with cheese and bacon.

recipes.name: Butter Burgers
recipes.description: The juiciest cheeseburger you will ever eat. Butter mixed right into the meat.

steps.name: Mix meat
steps.instruction: Combine ground chuck with softened butter and Holy Cow. Mix and form into four 1/3 lb patties.

steps.name: Cook
steps.instruction: Cook on hot griddle 4-5 minutes per side. Add cheese in final minute.

recipes.name: 0-400 Chicken Wings
recipes.description: Simple method for smoky yet crispy wings. Start cold, end hot.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Pat wings dry. Season with your choice of Meat Church rub.

steps.name: Cook
steps.instruction: Place wings on pellet grill while OFF. Turn on grill and set to 400°F. Cook until internal temp reaches 175°F with crispy skin, about 45-60 minutes.

recipes.name: Mexican Chicken Wings
recipes.description: Tailgate favorite using the Mexican technique with pickled jalapeño marinade.

steps.name: Marinate
steps.instruction: Place wings in container. Cover with pickled jalapeño juice. Marinate at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.

steps.name: Season and cook
steps.instruction: Remove from marinade, pat dry. Season with Dia de la Fajita. Smoke at 350°F until internal temp 175°F.

food.name: Meat Church Dia de la Fajita rub

recipes.name: Korean Fried Chicken Wings
recipes.description: Crispy double-fried wings tossed in sweet and spicy Korean sauce.

steps.name: Prep wings
steps.instruction: Pat wings very dry. Season with salt and pepper. Dredge in cornstarch.

steps.name: Double fry
steps.instruction: Fry at 325°F for 10 minutes. Rest 5 minutes. Fry again at 375°F for 5 minutes until crispy.

steps.name: Sauce
steps.instruction: Toss hot wings in Korean BBQ sauce.

recipes.name: Garlic Parmesan Chicken Wings
recipes.description: House favorite at Meat Church. Hands down the family's favorite wings.

steps.name: Season and cook
steps.instruction: Season wings with Garlic & Herb. Cook at 400°F until internal temp 175°F and skin is crispy.

steps.name: Toss in sauce
steps.instruction: Toss hot wings in garlic parmesan butter sauce. Top with grated parmesan.

recipes.name: Smoked Chicken with Alabama White Sauce
recipes.description: Spatchcock chicken dunked in tangy Alabama white sauce.

steps.name: Spatchcock
steps.instruction: Remove backbone from chicken with shears. Press flat. Season with Holy Cow on all sides, including under skin.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 300°F with hickory until internal temp 160°F in breast, about 1.5-2 hours. Baste with melted butter during cook.

steps.name: Sauce
steps.instruction: Dunk chicken in Alabama white sauce as soon as it comes off. Rest 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Pork Tenderloin
recipes.description: Honey Garlic Dijon pork tenderloin. Easy, versatile, and delicious.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Season pork tenderloin with Holy Cow.

steps.name: Cook
steps.instruction: Cook at 375°F until internal temp 140°F, about 30 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.

steps.name: Glaze
steps.instruction: Make glaze with honey, Dijon, and garlic. Drizzle over sliced tenderloin.

recipes.name: Whole Pork Loin
recipes.description: Affordable, versatile, and feeds a crowd. Great for meal prep.

steps.name: Brine and season
steps.instruction: Brine pork loin overnight. Pat dry. Season with Garlic & Herb.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 275°F until internal temp 140°F. Baste with herb butter during cook. Rest 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Reverse Seared Tri-Tip
recipes.description: Smoke then sear for the perfect tri-tip. Great for uneven cuts.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Season tri-tip with Holy Gospel, then add light coating of Garlic & Herb.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 225°F with oak, mesquite, hickory, or pecan until internal temp 115°F for medium-rare.

steps.name: Sear
steps.instruction: Sear over high heat 1-2 minutes per side. Rest 10 minutes before slicing against the grain.

recipes.name: The Ultimate Prime Rib
recipes.description: Smoke + sous vide method for the ultimate prime rib experience.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Apply heavy coat of salt, let sit 1 hour, rinse and pat dry. Slather with Worcestershire. Season liberally with Holy Cow and Garlic & Herb.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 200°F with oak, mesquite, or hickory until internal temp 120°F. Rest and sear if desired.

recipes.name: Smoked Prime Rib
recipes.description: All-time favorite meal. So easy and so dang good.

steps.name: Dry brine
steps.instruction: Apply heavy coat of salt. Let sit 1 hour. Wash off salt and pat very dry. Slather with Worcestershire as binder.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Season liberally with Holy Cow on all sides, then heavy coat of Garlic & Herb.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 250°F until internal temp 120°F for medium-rare. Rest 20-30 minutes before carving.

recipes.name: Smoked Turkey Breast
recipes.description: Great alternative to whole turkey. Easier to carve and presents beautifully.

steps.name: Prep and season
steps.instruction: Slather turkey breast with mayo as binder. Season liberally with Holy Cow or Texas Sugar.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 275°F with pecan, hickory, or fruit wood until internal temp 160°F. Rest 15 minutes.

steps.name: Glaze
steps.instruction: Optional: Apply honey glaze in final 30 minutes.

recipes.name: Traditional Smoked Turkey
recipes.description: Perfect smoked turkey for the holidays. Brined overnight for maximum moisture.

steps.name: Brine
steps.instruction: Brine turkey overnight using Meat Church brine. Average 1 hour per pound.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Remove from brine, pat very dry inside and out. Season with Holy Cow or your preferred rub.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 275°F, basting with melted butter periodically. Cook until breast reaches 160°F, about 3 hours for 14 lb bird.

recipes.name: Spatchcock Turkey
recipes.description: Cooks more evenly, presents beautifully, and easier to carve.

steps.name: Spatchcock
steps.instruction: Remove backbone with poultry shears. Press turkey flat, cracking breastbone. Season under skin and all over with Holy Cow.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 325°F until breast reaches 160°F, about 2-2.5 hours. Baste with butter.

recipes.name: Grilled Salmon
recipes.description: Staple in the Meat Church household. Rich in Omega-3s and great protein.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Pat salmon dry. Season with Garlic & Herb or Holy Voodoo for spicy version.

steps.name: Grill
steps.instruction: Grill over medium-high heat skin side down for 4-5 minutes. Flip and cook 3-4 more minutes until internal temp 145°F.

recipes.name: Smoked Queso Dip
recipes.description: Perfect party appetizer with smoky flavor. The ultimate tailgate dip.

steps.name: Cook meat
steps.instruction: Brown breakfast sausage in dutch oven and drain fat.

steps.name: Combine and smoke
steps.instruction: Add cubed Velveeta, smoked gouda, Rotel, and Holy Voodoo. Place uncovered on smoker at 350°F. Stir every 15 minutes until melted and combined, about 45 minutes.

recipes.name: Buffalo Chicken Dip
recipes.description: Easiest and tastiest dip. Load with smoked chicken for hearty tailgating.

steps.name: Mix ingredients
steps.instruction: Combine softened cream cheese, ranch dressing, buffalo sauce, and shredded chicken in baking dish.

steps.name: Bake
steps.instruction: Top with shredded cheese. Bake or smoke at 350°F until bubbly, about 25-30 minutes.

recipes.name: Country Style Ribs
recipes.description: BBQ classic. Not actually ribs but strips from pork butt or loin. Inexpensive and tasty.

steps.name: Season
steps.instruction: Season country style ribs with Honey Hog on all sides.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 275°F until internal temp 195°F for pull-apart tender, about 2.5-3 hours. Glaze with BBQ sauce if desired.

recipes.name: Beef Tips
recipes.description: Tender beef tips, great over rice or mashed potatoes.

steps.name: Season and sear
steps.instruction: Season beef tips with Holy Cow. Sear in hot cast iron with butter until browned on all sides.

steps.name: Braise
steps.instruction: Add beef broth and Worcestershire. Cover and braise at 300°F until tender, about 1.5-2 hours.

recipes.name: Pork Belly Burnt Ends
recipes.description: Sweet and sticky pork belly burnt ends - candy-like BBQ perfection.

steps.name: Cube and season
steps.instruction: Cut pork belly into 1.5 inch cubes. Season generously with Honey Hog Hot.

food.name: Meat Church Honey Hog Hot rub

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Smoke at 275°F for 2 hours until mahogany color develops.

steps.name: Braise and glaze
steps.instruction: Transfer to foil pan. Add butter, honey, and brown sugar. Cover and cook 1.5 hours. Uncover and glaze with BBQ sauce for final 30 minutes.

recipes.name: Smoked Mac and Cheese
recipes.description: Creamy, smoky mac and cheese with a crispy top - the ultimate BBQ side dish.

steps.name: Cook pasta
steps.instruction: Cook elbow macaroni to al dente. Drain and set aside.

steps.name: Make cheese sauce
steps.instruction: Melt butter, whisk in flour. Add milk and cream, simmer until thickened. Remove from heat, stir in cheeses until melted. Season with Holy Gospel.

steps.name: Smoke
steps.instruction: Combine pasta and sauce in cast iron or foil pan. Top with more shredded cheese. Smoke at 275°F for 1 hour until bubbly and top is golden.

recipes.name: Jalapeño Poppers
recipes.description: Bacon-wrapped jalapeño poppers stuffed with cream cheese - a BBQ party favorite.

steps.name: Prep jalapeños
steps.instruction: Halve jalapeños lengthwise, remove seeds and membranes.

steps.name: Make filling
steps.instruction: Mix cream cheese with shredded cheddar and Holy Voodoo. Fill each jalapeño half.

steps.name: Wrap and smoke
steps.instruction: Wrap each stuffed jalapeño with half a bacon slice. Smoke at 275°F for 45-60 minutes until bacon is crispy.
